acceptanceCriteria: The arrival-date picker on the Arrival details page renders with `data-min-date` set to 1 week before today and `data-max-date` set to 6 months after today, so the calendar offers only dates inside that window and dates outside it cannot be clicked.

Typing a date earlier than 1 week before today, or later than 6 months after today, into the arrival-date field and submitting re-renders the Arrival details page with a GDS error summary and an inline error against the arrival-date field; the rejected value is preserved in the input, the other answers on the page are preserved, and nothing is committed.
The boundary dates themselves — exactly 1 week before today and exactly 6 months after today — are accepted, so the window is inclusive at both ends.
A calendar-impossible arrival date such as 31/2/2026 still produces the existing 'Enter a real arrival date' message, not the out-of-range message.
A blank arrival date behaves exactly as it does today — the range rule does not turn the optional field into a required one.
With JavaScript disabled the arrival-date field is still an editable text input, and a typed in-window date saves and advances.
The stored arrival-date answer keeps its existing `{ day, month, year }` shape — `kit.readDate` and the committed value are unchanged.

The exit-date and add-a-document date-of-issue pickers are unchanged: their view models carry no `minDate`/`maxDate`, they still emit no restriction attributes, and they still accept any valid calendar date.
The out-of-range message and the reworded hint exist in both `copy.en.js` and `copy.cy.js` with identical structure, and `copy-parity.test.js` and `copy-convention.test.js` pass.
The arrival-date hint no longer offers an example date the field would reject; it states the allowed window instead.

No spec, fixture or test payload in either repo that passes an arrival date through the validator holds a hardcoded absolute date — every one is today-relative, so none rots as the wall clock advances.
